text:
Nora P: alert from observability — prefix-cache hit-rate for rwp-prod-7 dropped ~20% at 03:02 UTC. Paging the runtime crew.

Luis M: which metric specifically? is this KV prefix cache or the in-memory prefix-index?

Nora P: KV prefix cache (per-prefix kv_hits / lookups). Sample from grafana: 2026-03-18T03:02:10Z cluster=rwp-prod-7 kv_hit_rate=0.54 prev_1h=0.74

Priya S: Any rollouts around that window? Could be a deploy that changed prefix routing.

David R: I see a small canary for shard-rebalance was applied to prod pools at 02:50 (rollout id: rebalance-2026-03-18). It pushes new shard assignment decisions to reduce hot-shard skew.

Nora P: That aligns. I grabbed a pod trace (rwp-prod-7a) and noticed several handoff events and a flurry of cache misses for identical prefixes immediately after handoff.

Luis M: Do we have traces showing if cache entries were explicitly invalidated vs just not found on the new shard? Paste snippet.

Nora P: trace excerpt:
```
TS=2026-03-18T03:01:59Z pod=rwp-prod-7a
  event=shard_handoff prefix=svc:acct:550 -> target=shard-9
  event=update_routing ok
  event=cache_miss prefix=svc:acct:550
  event=get_from_persistent_store latency=12ms
  event=store_to_cache
```
No explicit delete call in that snippet, but there are lots of misses right after handoff.

Priya S: If the new shard didn't receive the cached KV items, either the handoff didn't transfer the cache (by design) or the persistent-store reads are slower/blocked during handoff causing recovery delay.

David R: The rebalance change had an optimization to avoid copying large KV blobs during handoff; it relied on on-demand fetch from the backing store. That speeds handoff but will create a cold cache on target shard until requests repopulate it.

Luis M: That could explain transient drops, but 20% sustained is concerning. How long has the low hit-rate persisted?

Nora P: Currently ~22 minutes and not trending back up.

qa-bot: repro request created: run kv_hotset_repro on rwp-test-9 with skew pattern: heavy-hot-keys-5k.json (ETA 10m)

Priya S: Can we simulate the rebalance in a test pool with more aggressive traffic to see recovery curve? If on-demand fetch is the approach, we need to ensure fetch latency and persistent store QPS are sufficient.

David R: Good point. I can run a bench with two modes: (A) copy-on-handoff (old behavior) and (B) on-demand fetch (new behavior). Command I'm using:
```
./tools/kv_rebalance_bench --target rwp-test-9 --mode=ondemand --duration=900 --hotkeys=5000
./tools/kv_rebalance_bench --target rwp-test-9 --mode=copy --duration=900 --hotkeys=5000
```
I'll post numbers in ~20m.

Luis M: Also check persistent-store metrics (read latency, QPS) during those runs. If reads spike and latency increases, on-demand might cause cascading effects.

Nora P: I'm adding an alert tweak: if per-prefix miss-rate > 0.2 for > 10m on any prod pool, escalate to oncall.

deploy-bot: rollout rebalance-2026-03-18 paused by request from Luis M. Reason: investigate sustained cache degradation.

David R: Bench results (rwp-test-9): mode=ondemand -> initial hit-rate drop to 0.52 then recovery to 0.68 over 12 minutes. mode=copy -> drop to 0.70 then back to 0.72 in 3 minutes. Persistent-store read latency in ondemand jumped from 4ms -> 18ms during warmup.

Priya S: So copy reduces cold-start pain but adds traffic and longer handoff duration. Ondemand keeps handoff fast but amplifies persistent-store load and prolongs recovery.

Luis M: For production hot prefixes we should prefer copy-on-handoff. Maybe we can make the rebalance choose strategy per-prefix based on recent QPS/hitrate. High-QPS prefixes copy, low-QPS use ondemand.

Nora P: That seems reasonable. Action items:
- David: add per-prefix strategy feature flag and revert prod canary to copy-mode until strategy lands (ETA experiment branch in PR)
- Priya: add benchmark test to CI that simulates rebalance with hotset and validates hit-rate recovery time under 10 minutes
- Luis: keep rollout paused; coordinate canary once copy-mode patch merged

David R: Opening PR with feature-flag and a quick default to copy for prefixes with qps>10: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8490

qa-bot: test run queued for PR 8490: kv-rebalance-e2e (ETA 25m)

Nora P: Thanks all. Once CI green, we'll merge and roll copy-mode to the paused canary for rwp-prod-7 and monitor. Leaving the thread open until canary stabilizes.
